text:
morgan: Kicking off a late-wave, timezone-aware rollout. Plan: US -> EU -> APAC. Window starts 23:00 PT. Need a final capacity + rollback checklist. @deploy-bot do we have the canary slices ready?

deploy-bot: Canary slices allocated: us-small (5 GPUs), eu-small (3 GPUs), apac-small (2 GPUs). Will start US canary at 23:00 PT. Logs and status posted to deploy stream. :rocket:

yana: Quick capacity readout — current reserved pool utilization: US 72%, EU 58%, APAC 41%. Warm pool has 12 GPUs in US, 6 in EU, 4 in APAC. If US canary spikes >15% sustained, warm pool can backfill for ~6 minutes at current throughput.

devon: Noted. The new quantized runtime (rdx-q-v3) increases single-request memory by ~60MB on 32k contexts under 8-bit path; thermal numbers look fine in EU but US infra nodes are tighter. Recommend restricting max-concurrency to 8 for US canary.

morgan: Ok - set max-concurrency=8 for US slice. Pin version to `rdx-q-v3-2026-03-21` for canary. Sam — release notes (short) ready? Need token-cost blurb + fallback behavior.

sam: Release notes draft: "rdx-q-v3 lowers per-token latency 8-12% at SLOs, may increase memory use on long contexts; automatic fallback to rdx-legacy-cpu when GPU OOMs detected."
Add to notes: how to opt-out via `x-redwood-pin: rdx-legacy` header.

oncall: Watch plan: 60m watch in US after canary start. Escalation at >=5% error rate or p95 latency regression >120ms vs baseline for 3 consecutive 5-min windows. If triggered, immediate pin to previous `rdx-q-v2` and stop rollout. I’ll be on standby.

izzy: Quick checklist I pushed to ops-runbook:
- Canary start US: 23:00 PT
- Verify p50/p95/p99 heatmap within first 10m
- Confirm warm-pool fill threshold < 80%
- If CPU fallback >0.5% of requests, pause rollout
- Post rollout notes + metrics to #releases
(links: https://internal.runbook/late-wave)

morgan: Good. Also add a soft-threshold: if model-serving token-cost per-second increases >10% sustained, rollback. Cost alert path is integrated with billing watch.

deploy-bot: Running preflight smoke:
```
deploy-bot: smoke-check --slice us --model rdx-q-v3-2026-03-21 --max-concurrency 8
status: PASS (latency p95 190ms, errors 0.2%)
```

yana: Preflight numbers align. US heat baseline: p95 180-200ms during tests. Warm-pool headroom is ~9 GPUs if we drain and reassign.

devon: One more thing — EU has an overlapping maintenance window tomorrow 02:00 CET; we should avoid activating EU slice during that overlap. Shift EU start +90m after US verification.

morgan: Good catch. New plan: US canary 23:00 PT -> monitor 60m -> EU start earliest +90m after US start (so ~01:30 PT?), APAC only after EU 60m green.

sam: I'm tagging the release notes with the pinned header example and the fallback paragraph. Will publish to the docs page after US green.

oncall: I'll create temporary alerts:
- alert: rdq_err_rate_us (threshold 5%)
- alert: rdq_p95_regression_us (threshold +120ms)
Add slack webhook to this thread.

morgan: If anything looks off and we need to rollback, use the explicit command `deploy-bot rollback --slice <region> --to rdx-q-v2` and then pin global traffic to `rdx-q-v2` until manual approval. No partial quiet rollbacks; prefer full-slice stop + pin.

izzy: Putting a secondary safety: if warm-pool backfill latency > 300ms for 2 windows, we auto-hold rollout.

yana: Scheduled capacity hold windows posted to ops dashboard. Also setting short-lived quota increase for US warm pool if needed (approval required from capacity@redwood).

morgan: Thanks. Final runbook steps — I’ll trigger the deploy at 23:00 PT and @oncall starts monitoring. Please react with :eyes: when you’re watching.

sam: :eyes:

izzy: :eyes: monitoring dashboards up

deploy-bot: US canary start queued for 23:00 PT. ETA logs available in 2m.

morgan: Closing the loop — will post a concise postmortem if we hit rollback. Otherwise I’ll drop a short summary once APAC finishes. GL everyone. :thumbsup:
